## ⚠️ Important: GoDaddy cPanel shared hosting will NOT work for this app

Your project's hosting doc ([docs/19-hosting-and-domains.md](docs/19-hosting-and-domains.md)) **explicitly** evaluated GoDaddy cPanel's "Setup Node.js App" feature and ruled it out. Here's why it genuinely can't run this app:

| Blocker | Why cPanel/shared hosting fails |
|---|---|
| **Build memory** | The Next.js + Payload build needs **~4 GB RAM**; shared cPanel plans cap a process at ~1 GB. The build will crash. |
| **Node version** | Requires **Node 22.12+** (`package.json` engines). cPanel's "Setup Node.js App" selector often doesn't offer Node 22. |
| **Background jobs** | The app runs always-on scheduled jobs (`jobs.autoRun`). cPanel uses Phusion Passenger, which stops/starts the app on demand — jobs won't run reliably. |
| **No Docker / no root** | Your deployment is built around the Docker image + standalone Next.js output. |
| **Multi-tenancy** | Each vendor domain must pass the original `Host` header through a reverse proxy to one shared app. cPanel addon domains don't do this cleanly, and are capped per plan. |
| **No MongoDB** | Not included — you'd need MongoDB Atlas regardless. |

**The good news:** If you bought a **GoDaddy VPS** (not shared/cPanel hosting), it's a normal Ubuntu Linux server with root — and the doc has a complete, working VPS deployment guide. That's the path a pipeline should target.

Thank you — that's the key detail. Let me give you a direct, honest answer.

## Short answer: cPanel "Node.js App" will NOT reliably work for this app. You need a VPS.

Even though cPanel offers a "Setup Node.js App" feature, **this specific app** (Next.js 16 + Payload CMS 3 + multi-tenant) does not fit within what cPanel shared/Node.js hosting can do. Here's the concrete reasoning mapped to your actual code:

### Why cPanel Node.js hosting fails for *this* app

| Requirement (from your code) | cPanel Node.js reality | Result |
|---|---|---|
| **Build needs ~4 GB RAM** — `next build` + Payload ([Dockerfile](docker/Dockerfile) builds in a 4GB-swap VPS per docs/19) | Shared plans cap a process at ~512 MB–1 GB | ❌ Build gets killed (OOM) |
| **Node 22.12+** — `"node": ">=22.12.0 <23"` in [package.json](package.json) | cPanel's Node selector usually tops out below 22 | ❌ Won't start / wrong runtime |
| **Always-on background jobs** — `jobs.autoRun` in `src/payload.config.ts` | Phusion Passenger sleeps/restarts the app on demand | ❌ Scheduled publishing, subscription checks silently stop |
| **Host-header reverse proxy** — multi-tenant routing in `src/proxy.ts` reads the original `Host` header | Passenger doesn't let you pass raw `Host` for wildcard + vendor domains | ❌ Vendor domains won't map to the right store |
| **Standalone server** — [next.config.ts](next.config.ts) uses `output: 'standalone'` (expects `node server.js`) | cPanel expects a single entry file + `node_modules` install on the box | ⚠️ Fragile; the `pnpm install` of Payload native deps (sharp, esbuild) often fails on shared hosts |
| **Wildcard subdomains** `*.tenantecom.in` for every store | cPanel addon/subdomains are manual and capped per plan | ❌ Doesn't scale per vendor |
| **MongoDB replica set** (Payload transactions) | Not provided by cPanel | ❌ Need Atlas anyway |

2. **Vercel + Atlas** — the originally recorded decision (docs/00); least ops effort.

Content:
# 19 Hosting and domains

How to put the app on a server, what it needs, whether GoDaddy works, and how each vendor's store
address and CMS address reach the right store. Written 4 October 2026; nothing is deployed yet
(docs/progress.md).

Examples use `tenantecom.in` as the platform domain, `203.0.113.10` as the server's IP address and
Home Orbit (slug `home-orbit`) with an own domain `homeorbit.in`. Swap in the real values.

## What the app needs

One Next.js + Payload app serves every store, the vendor CMS and the platform panel (docs/01). It
needs:

| Need | What exactly | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Node.js | 22.12 or later, below 23 (`package.json` engines) | The Docker image brings its own |
| Memory | About 1 GB for the running app; about 4 GB while building | Build somewhere else, or add swap on a small server |
| MongoDB | A **replica set** (Payload uses transactions) | MongoDB Atlas, Mumbai region: M10 for production, the free M0 is fine for a trial |
| Object storage | An S3-compatible bucket + a public CDN address | Cloudflare R2 recommended (docs/12). Needed on a server too: a container's disk is replaced on every update (the app only warns at boot outside Vercel, `src/lib/mediaStorage.ts`) |
| Email | Resend API key with the sending domain verified | Staff invites and password resets |
| Domain | A platform domain you control | Must not contain "sr", "kr" or "shiprocket" (docs/open-items) |
| HTTPS | A certificate for the admin address, every store subdomain and every vendor domain | Caddy (below) gets and renews them automatically |
| Reverse proxy | Something in front of the app on ports 80/443 that **passes the original `Host` header** | The app picks the store from that header |
| Always-on process | The app runs background jobs on a timer (`jobs.autoRun` in `src/payload.config.ts`) | Fine on a VPS; serverless hosts need a cron instead |

Environment variables are all in `.env.example`. For production:

```bash
NODE_ENV=production
DATABASE_URI=mongodb+srv://<user>:<password>@<cluster>.mongodb.net/tenantecom?retryWrites=true&w=majority
PAYLOAD_SECRET=<openssl rand -hex 32>
ADMIN_URL=https://admin.tenantecom.in
PLATFORM_DOMAIN=tenantecom.in
RESEND_API_KEY=<from Resend>
EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS=no-reply@tenantecom.in
EMAIL_FROM_NAME=TenantEcom
S3_BUCKET=tenantecom-media
S3_ENDPOINT=https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com
S3_REGION=auto
S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID=<R2 token id>
S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=<R2 token secret>
MEDIA_PUBLIC_URL=https://media.tenantecom.in
S3_CLIENT_UPLOADS=false
```

No quotes around values (Docker's `--env-file` keeps quotes as part of the value).

## Where to host it

| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Vercel + Atlas | The recorded decision (docs/00, docs/02). Least work to run; custom domains get SSL automatically. Short notes at the end of this file |
| **A Linux VPS** (GoDaddy VPS, AWS Lightsail Mumbai, DigitalOcean Bangalore, any other) + Atlas | Works, using the Docker image we already keep building (docs/15). Step by step below |
| GoDaddy shared hosting (cPanel "Setup Node.js App") | **Not suitable.** See the next section |

If the team picks a VPS over Vercel for production, record that in docs/00 "Decisions" (CLAUDE.md:
the stack does not change without a recorded decision).

## Can it run on GoDaddy?

**GoDaddy shared hosting / cPanel Node.js: no.** Those plans run small Node apps through Phusion
Passenger with tight limits, and this app does not fit:

- The build needs about 4 GB of memory; shared plans cap a process at around 1 GB or less.
- The Node versions on offer may not include Node 22, which this app requires.
- Passenger starts and stops the app on demand, so the background jobs (scheduled publishing,
 subscription checks, later payments and parcel jobs) would not run reliably.
- No root and no Docker; each vendor's own domain would have to be added as an "addon domain",
 limited per plan, and pointed at the same app by hand.
- MongoDB is not included (Atlas would still be needed).

**GoDaddy VPS: yes.** A self-managed GoDaddy VPS is an ordinary Linux server with root access, so
the steps below work as written. Pick:

- Ubuntu 24.04 LTS
- 2 vCPU and 4 GB RAM at least (8 GB if you build on the same server without swap)
- 40 GB+ disk
- The data centre closest to India that GoDaddy offers. The database sits in Atlas Mumbai, and
 every page makes database calls, so the server should be close to Mumbai. If GoDaddy has no
 nearby location, a Mumbai or Bangalore VPS from another provider is the better choice; the steps
 are the same.

Buying the domain from GoDaddy is fine with any of the options; only the DNS records matter.

## Step by step: a Linux VPS

### 1. Accounts to create first

1. **Platform domain** (for example `tenantecom.in`).
2. **MongoDB Atlas**: create a cluster in AWS Mumbai (`ap-south-1`). Add a database user. Under
 Network Access add the server's IP address (and your own, for step 7). Copy the `mongodb+srv://`
 connection string into `DATABASE_URI`.
3. **Cloudflare R2**: create a bucket (for example `tenantecom-media`), an API token with read and
 write on it, and connect a custom domain to the bucket (for example `media.tenantecom.in`) for
 `MEDIA_PUBLIC_URL`.
4. **Resend**: verify the sending domain, create an API key.

### 2. DNS for the platform domain

In GoDaddy (Domain, DNS, Manage DNS) for `tenantecom.in`:

| Type | Name | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `admin` | `203.0.113.10` | Platform panel and every vendor's CMS |
| A | `*` | `203.0.113.10` | Every store subdomain (`home-orbit.tenantecom.in`, ...) without a DNS change per vendor |
| A | `@` | `203.0.113.10` | The bare domain (redirected to the admin for now, see step 6) |

`media` is set up by Cloudflare when you connect the R2 custom domain (the domain's DNS must be on
Cloudflare for that; otherwise use R2's public `r2.dev` address or put a CDN in front).

### 3. Prepare the server

```bash
ssh root@203.0.113.10
adduser deploy && usermod -aG sudo deploy # work as this user from now on
apt update && apt upgrade -y
ufw allow OpenSSH && ufw allow 80 && ufw allow 443 && ufw enable

# Swap, so building on a 4 GB server does not run out of memory
fallocate -l 4G /swapfile && chmod 600 /swapfile && mkswap /swapfile && swapon /swapfile
echo '/swapfile none swap sw 0 0' >> /etc/fstab

# Docker
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh
usermod -aG docker deploy
```

Log in again as `deploy`.

### 4. Get the code and the settings

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /opt/tenantecom && sudo chown deploy /opt/tenantecom
cd /opt/tenantecom
git clone https://github.com/mudit06/tenantcommerce.git app # a deploy key or token for a private repo
nano /opt/tenantecom/.env.production # the variables from the top of this file
chmod 600 /opt/tenantecom/.env.production
```

The settings file lives outside the git checkout and is never committed (CLAUDE.md rule 9).

### 5. Build and start the app

```bash
cd /opt/tenantecom/app
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t tenantecom:latest .
docker run -d --name tenantecom --restart unless-stopped \
 --env-file /opt/tenantecom/.env.production \
 -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \
 tenantecom:latest
docker logs -f tenantecom # wait for "Ready", then Ctrl+C
```

`127.0.0.1:3000` keeps the app reachable only through Caddy, never directly from the internet.

### 6. HTTPS and the `Host` header: Caddy

Caddy terminates HTTPS, gets a free Let's Encrypt certificate for every address it lists, renews
them, and passes the original `Host` header to the app (which is how the app knows the store).

```bash
sudo apt install -y debian-keyring debian-archive-keyring apt-transport-https curl
curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/gpg.key' | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/caddy-stable-archive-keyring.gpg
curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/debian.deb.txt' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/caddy-stable.list
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y caddy
```

`/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`:

```caddyfile
{
	email ops@tenantecom.in
}

(app) {
	reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
}

# Platform panel and every vendor's CMS
admin.tenantecom.in {
	import app
}

# Bare platform domain: no marketing site yet
tenantecom.in, www.tenantecom.in {
	redir https://admin.tenantecom.in/admin 302
}

# ---- Stores: one block per store ----
# Home Orbit: platform subdomain and its own domain
home-orbit.tenantecom.in, homeorbit.in {
	import app
}
www.homeorbit.in {
	redir https://homeorbit.in{uri} 301
}
cms.homeorbit.in {
	redir https://admin.tenantecom.in/admin 302
}
```

```bash
sudo systemctl reload caddy
```

Caddy needs each address to already point at the server (DNS) and ports 80 and 443 open before it
can get the certificate. `journalctl -u caddy -f` shows progress.

If you use nginx instead of Caddy, keep `proxy_set_header Host $host;` and raise
`client_max_body_size` to 50m (catalogue PDFs, `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` in `src/payload.config.ts`).

### 7. First data

The production image holds only the built app, not the seed scripts, so run the seed once from a
developer machine (a full checkout with `pnpm install`) pointed at the production database. Copy
the production values into a git-ignored file, for example `.env.production.local`, add
`SEED_SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL` and a strong `SEED_SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, then:

```bash
set -a && source .env.production.local && set +a
NODE_ENV=development pnpm seed # plans, the first super admin, 2 demo stores (draft)
NODE_ENV=development pnpm seed:home-orbit # only if Home Orbit's catalogue should be loaded
```

Variables already in the shell win over `.env`, so this writes to Atlas and R2, not to your local
setup. `PLATFORM_DOMAIN` must be the real one here, because new stores get
`<slug>.<PLATFORM_DOMAIN>` as their first address. The demo stores stay in draft and show "coming
soon" in production; archive them from the platform panel if you don't want them.

### 8. Check it

1. `https://admin.tenantecom.in` opens the admin login; sign in as the super admin and change the
 password.
2. `https://home-orbit.tenantecom.in` shows "Home Orbit is coming soon" while the store is in
 draft. Go live from the platform panel (vendor overview, Go live) and reload.
3. Upload an image in the CMS and check its address starts with `MEDIA_PUBLIC_URL`.
4. Walk docs/manual-testing.md against the live addresses.

### 9. Updates

```bash
cd /opt/tenantecom/app && git pull
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t tenantecom:latest .
docker rm -f tenantecom && docker run -d --name tenantecom --restart unless-stopped \
 --env-file /opt/tenantecom/.env.production -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 tenantecom:latest
```

The store is down for the few seconds between `rm` and `run`. When that matters, build the image in
CI, push it to a registry, and switch between two containers behind Caddy. Run Payload migrations
(docs/15) before starting a new version once there are any. Backups are Atlas's (docs/15).

### Without Docker (Node + PM2)

Works too; Docker is preferred because CI keeps the image building (docs/15).

```bash
# Node 22 from NodeSource, then pnpm through corepack
curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_22.x | sudo -E bash - && sudo apt install -y nodejs
sudo corepack enable && sudo npm install -g pm2

cd /opt/tenantecom/app && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
set -a && source /opt/tenantecom/.env.production && set +a && pnpm build
cp -r public .next/standalone/ && cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/
PORT=3000 HOSTNAME=127.0.0.1 pm2 start .next/standalone/server.js --name tenantecom \
 --node-args="--env-file=/opt/tenantecom/.env.production"
pm2 save && pm2 startup # restart on reboot
```

Caddy (step 6) stays the same.

## How vendor addresses reach the right store

There is no per-vendor server and nothing redirects a shopper between stores. Every address
points at the **same app**, and the app reads which address was asked for:

```
 shopper -> https://homeorbit.in/products/basin-mixer
 DNS: homeorbit.in -> 203.0.113.10 (our server)
 Caddy: HTTPS, passes Host: homeorbit.in to the app
 src/proxy.ts: host is not the admin host -> rewrite (not redirect) to /homeorbit.in/products/basin-mixer
 src/lib/data/store.ts getStoreByHost('homeorbit.in'): tenant-domains -> Home Orbit
 src/app/(storefront)/[tenant]: Home Orbit's pages, its data only, its look from
 src/storefront/vendors/home-orbit/

 vendor staff -> https://admin.tenantecom.in/admin
 src/proxy.ts: admin host -> Payload admin
 signed in as Home Orbit staff -> only Home Orbit's CMS (workspaces and access, docs/05)
```

| Address | What it shows | Where it is set |
|---|---|---|
| `admin.tenantecom.in` | Platform panel for our team; the store's CMS for vendor staff | `ADMIN_URL` |
| `<slug>.tenantecom.in` | That vendor's store | Created automatically when the vendor is onboarded (`tenant-domains`, primary) |
| Vendor's own domain | That vendor's store | Added by a super admin in `tenant-domains` (below) |
| Any other address | 404 page | |

The address-to-store map is cached for up to 5 minutes and cleared whenever a domain changes
(docs/04).

### A new vendor's store subdomain

Nothing to do in DNS (the `*` record covers it). Onboard the vendor (New vendor screen or
`pnpm create-tenant`); the store answers on `<slug>.tenantecom.in`. On a VPS add the address to
the Caddyfile so it gets a certificate, then `sudo systemctl reload caddy`.

### A vendor's own domain (for example `homeorbit.in`)

1. **Vendor's DNS** (at their registrar; GoDaddy shown):

 | Type | Name | Value |
 |---|---|---|
 | A | `@` | `203.0.113.10` |
 | CNAME | `www` | `home-orbit.tenantecom.in` |

 GoDaddy can't put a CNAME on the bare domain, so `@` is an A record to the server's IP. If the
 server's IP ever changes, every vendor's `@` record has to change too; a fixed IP for the
 server avoids that.

2. **Tell the app the domain belongs to the store.** Custom domains have no form yet (the
 Domains tab marks it Phase 2). A super admin, in the platform panel (no store session open),
 opens `https://admin.tenantecom.in/admin/collections/tenant-domains/create` and adds `homeorbit.in`:
 tenant Home Orbit, type Custom, Primary ticked (making it primary unticks the subdomain). Add
 `www.homeorbit.in` the same way, not primary, if the store should also answer there instead of
 Caddy redirecting it.

3. **Certificate and routing**: add the domain to the Caddyfile (step 6) and reload Caddy.

4. **One address for search engines**: links, the sitemap and robots.txt use whichever address
 the shopper opened. The stored "redirect to primary" flag is not acted on yet
 (docs/open-items "Primary domain redirect"), so redirect the other addresses in Caddy:
 `www.homeorbit.in` to `homeorbit.in` as above, and, once the vendor's domain is live, the
 subdomain too:

 ```caddyfile
 homeorbit.in {
 	import app
 }
 home-orbit.tenantecom.in, www.homeorbit.in {
 	redir https://homeorbit.in{uri} 301
 }
 ```

### The vendor CMS address

Every vendor signs in at the one admin address, `https://admin.tenantecom.in/admin`. The account
decides what opens: a store's staff get that store's CMS and never see another store; our team
gets the platform panel and reaches a store's CMS only through "Manage store" or "View as support"
(docs/05 "As built"). In production
the admin works only on `ADMIN_URL` (`src/proxy.ts`, CSRF list in
`src/payload.config.ts`).

A vendor who wants a CMS address on their own domain can have a **redirect**: `cms.homeorbit.in`
to `https://admin.tenantecom.in/admin` (the Caddy block above; the vendor adds an A record for
`cms` pointing to the server). Serving the admin itself on each vendor's domain (white-label CMS)
would need code changes (admin host list, CSRF list, sign-in cookies per domain) and is not
planned; raise it in docs/open-items before building it.

## Notes for Vercel instead

- Import the GitHub repo as a Vercel project and set the environment variables, plus
 `S3_CLIENT_UPLOADS=true` (Vercel caps request bodies at 4.5 MB; the bucket needs a CORS rule
 allowing PUT from the admin address).
- Wildcard subdomains (`*.tenantecom.in`) on Vercel need the domain's nameservers moved to Vercel.
- Each vendor domain is added to the project (Settings, Domains); Vercel shows the DNS records and
 issues the certificate. Add the same host to `tenant-domains` as above.
- Background jobs don't run on a timer there: a Vercel Cron for `/api/payload-jobs/run` is still
 to be configured (docs/progress.md, Platform foundations).
- Pick the Mumbai (`bom1`) function region, next to Atlas.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause |
|---|---|
| A store address shows the 404 page | The host is not in `tenant-domains` (check `www.` too), or the store is archived |
| "coming soon" on a store | The store is still in draft: Go live in the platform panel |
| Admin sign-in loops back to the login page | The address in the browser is not exactly `ADMIN_URL`, or `ADMIN_URL` is `http://` while the site is on HTTPS |
| Caddy can't get a certificate | DNS for that address does not point at the server yet, or port 80/443 is closed |
| Uploads fail | `S3_*` variables missing or wrong; the container can't store files on its own disk |
| `MongoServerSelectionError` in `docker logs` | The server's IP is not in Atlas Network Access, or `DATABASE_URI` is wrong |
| The app stops on a small server during build | Not enough memory: add swap (step 3) or build the image elsewhere |

# Multi-stage build on Next standalone output (docs/15). Same Node major as local and Vercel.
FROM node:22-alpine AS base
RUN corepack enable
WORKDIR /app

FROM base AS deps
COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml ./
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

FROM base AS builder
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY . .
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1
# Placeholders so env validation passes at build time; real values come from the runtime
# environment and are never baked into the image
RUN PAYLOAD_SECRET=build-time-placeholder-not-a-secret-0000000000 \
 DATABASE_URI=mongodb://localhost:27017/build \
 pnpm build

FROM node:22-alpine AS runner
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 PORT=3000 HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0
RUN addgroup -S nodejs && adduser -S nextjs -G nodejs
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/static ./.next/static
# Standalone output leaves public/ out; without it /favicon.svg and other root files 404
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/public ./public
USER nextjs
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "server.js"]

Perfect! I have all the details from your own hosting documentation. Let me give you the **exact VPS specifications** researched and validated for your TenantEcom application.

---

## VPS Server Specifications for TenantEcom

Based on your project's hosting documentation ([docs/19-hosting-and-domains.md](docs/19-hosting-and-domains.md)), here are the **exact requirements**:

### ✅ Minimum VPS Specifications

| Component | Requirement | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Operating System** | **Ubuntu 24.04 LTS** | Tested and documented in your setup guide |
| **CPU** | **2 vCPU** minimum | Handles Next.js build + runtime + background jobs |
| **RAM** | **4 GB** minimum | Running app needs ~1 GB; build needs ~4 GB |
| **Storage** | **40 GB+** disk | Docker images, app code, logs, swap file |
| **Swap** | **4 GB swap file** | Critical if building on the server (prevents out-of-memory crashes during `next build`) |
| **Network** | **Ports 80, 443, 22** open | HTTPS (Caddy), SSH access |
| **Location** | **Closest to Mumbai/India** | Your MongoDB Atlas is in **AWS Mumbai (ap-south-1)** — low latency is critical for every page load |

---

### Scaling Notes

| Scenario | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| **Build separately** (CI/CD builds Docker image, VPS only runs it) | Can drop to **2 GB RAM** on VPS (no swap needed) |
| **High traffic** (100+ vendors or 10K+ daily visitors) | Upgrade to **4 vCPU / 8 GB RAM** |
| **Production-grade** | **8 GB RAM** if you skip swap and want headroom |

---

### Recommended VPS Providers (India-focused)

Since your database is in **Mumbai**, pick the **geographically closest** option:

| Provider | Plan | Location | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **GoDaddy VPS** | Self-managed, 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 40 GB | Check if they offer **Mumbai or Singapore** | Your docs explicitly validate GoDaddy VPS works |
| **AWS Lightsail** | $20/month, 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 80 GB SSD | **Mumbai (ap-south-1)** | Same region as Atlas — lowest latency |
| **DigitalOcean** | $24/month, 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 80 GB | **Bangalore (blr1)** | Close to Mumbai, excellent docs |
| **Hetzner** | €4.49/month, 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 40 GB | **No India datacenter** | Cheapest but high latency to Mumbai Atlas |

**Best choice:** AWS Lightsail Mumbai or DigitalOcean Bangalore — both are **in India** and close to your Atlas cluster.

---

# 19 Hosting and domains

How to put the app on a server, what it needs, whether GoDaddy works, and how each vendor's store
address and CMS address reach the right store. Written 4 October 2026; nothing is deployed yet
(docs/progress.md).

Examples use `tenantecom.in` as the platform domain, `203.0.113.10` as the server's IP address and
Home Orbit (slug `home-orbit`) with an own domain `homeorbit.in`. Swap in the real values.

## What the app needs

One Next.js + Payload app serves every store, the vendor CMS and the platform panel (docs/01). It
needs:

| Need | What exactly | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Node.js | 22.12 or later, below 23 (`package.json` engines) | The Docker image brings its own |
| Memory | About 1 GB for the running app; about 4 GB while building | Build somewhere else, or add swap on a small server |
| MongoDB | A **replica set** (Payload uses transactions) | MongoDB Atlas, Mumbai region: M10 for production, the free M0 is fine for a trial |
| Object storage | An S3-compatible bucket + a public CDN address | Cloudflare R2 recommended (docs/12). Needed on a server too: a container's disk is replaced on every update (the app only warns at boot outside Vercel, `src/lib/mediaStorage.ts`) |
| Email | Resend API key with the sending domain verified | Staff invites and password resets |
| Domain | A platform domain you control | Must not contain "sr", "kr" or "shiprocket" (docs/open-items) |
| HTTPS | A certificate for the admin address, every store subdomain and every vendor domain | Caddy (below) gets and renews them automatically |
| Reverse proxy | Something in front of the app on ports 80/443 that **passes the original `Host` header** | The app picks the store from that header |
| Always-on process | The app runs background jobs on a timer (`jobs.autoRun` in `src/payload.config.ts`) | Fine on a VPS; serverless hosts need a cron instead |

Environment variables are all in `.env.example`. For production:

```bash
NODE_ENV=production
DATABASE_URI=mongodb+srv://<user>:<password>@<cluster>.mongodb.net/tenantecom?retryWrites=true&w=majority
PAYLOAD_SECRET=<openssl rand -hex 32>
ADMIN_URL=https://admin.tenantecom.in
PLATFORM_DOMAIN=tenantecom.in
RESEND_API_KEY=<from Resend>
EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS=no-reply@tenantecom.in
EMAIL_FROM_NAME=TenantEcom
S3_BUCKET=tenantecom-media
S3_ENDPOINT=https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com
S3_REGION=auto
S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID=<R2 token id>
S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=<R2 token secret>
MEDIA_PUBLIC_URL=https://media.tenantecom.in
S3_CLIENT_UPLOADS=false
```

No quotes around values (Docker's `--env-file` keeps quotes as part of the value).

## Where to host it

| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Vercel + Atlas | The recorded decision (docs/00, docs/02). Least work to run; custom domains get SSL automatically. Short notes at the end of this file |
| **A Linux VPS** (GoDaddy VPS, AWS Lightsail Mumbai, DigitalOcean Bangalore, any other) + Atlas | Works, using the Docker image we already keep building (docs/15). Step by step below |
| GoDaddy shared hosting (cPanel "Setup Node.js App") | **Not suitable.** See the next section |

If the team picks a VPS over Vercel for production, record that in docs/00 "Decisions" (CLAUDE.md:
the stack does not change without a recorded decision).

## Can it run on GoDaddy?

**GoDaddy shared hosting / cPanel Node.js: no.** Those plans run small Node apps through Phusion
Passenger with tight limits, and this app does not fit:

- The build needs about 4 GB of memory; shared plans cap a process at around 1 GB or less.
- The Node versions on offer may not include Node 22, which this app requires.
- Passenger starts and stops the app on demand, so the background jobs (scheduled publishing,
 subscription checks, later payments and parcel jobs) would not run reliably.
- No root and no Docker; each vendor's own domain would have to be added as an "addon domain",
 limited per plan, and pointed at the same app by hand.
- MongoDB is not included (Atlas would still be needed).

**GoDaddy VPS: yes.** A self-managed GoDaddy VPS is an ordinary Linux server with root access, so
the steps below work as written. Pick:

- Ubuntu 24.04 LTS
- 2 vCPU and 4 GB RAM at least (8 GB if you build on the same server without swap)
- 40 GB+ disk
- The data centre closest to India that GoDaddy offers. The database sits in Atlas Mumbai, and
 every page makes database calls, so the server should be close to Mumbai. If GoDaddy has no
 nearby location, a Mumbai or Bangalore VPS from another provider is the better choice; the steps
 are the same.

Buying the domain from GoDaddy is fine with any of the options; only the DNS records matter.

## Step by step: a Linux VPS

### 1. Accounts to create first

1. **Platform domain** (for example `tenantecom.in`).
2. **MongoDB Atlas**: create a cluster in AWS Mumbai (`ap-south-1`). Add a database user. Under
 Network Access add the server's IP address (and your own, for step 7). Copy the `mongodb+srv://`
 connection string into `DATABASE_URI`.
3. **Cloudflare R2**: create a bucket (for example `tenantecom-media`), an API token with read and
 write on it, and connect a custom domain to the bucket (for example `media.tenantecom.in`) for
 `MEDIA_PUBLIC_URL`.
4. **Resend**: verify the sending domain, create an API key.

### 2. DNS for the platform domain

In GoDaddy (Domain, DNS, Manage DNS) for `tenantecom.in`:

| Type | Name | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `admin` | `203.0.113.10` | Platform panel and every vendor's CMS |
| A | `*` | `203.0.113.10` | Every store subdomain (`home-orbit.tenantecom.in`, ...) without a DNS change per vendor |
| A | `@` | `203.0.113.10` | The bare domain (redirected to the admin for now, see step 6) |

`media` is set up by Cloudflare when you connect the R2 custom domain (the domain's DNS must be on
Cloudflare for that; otherwise use R2's public `r2.dev` address or put a CDN in front).

### 3. Prepare the server

```bash
ssh root@203.0.113.10
adduser deploy && usermod -aG sudo deploy # work as this user from now on
apt update && apt upgrade -y
ufw allow OpenSSH && ufw allow 80 && ufw allow 443 && ufw enable

# Swap, so building on a 4 GB server does not run out of memory
fallocate -l 4G /swapfile && chmod 600 /swapfile && mkswap /swapfile && swapon /swapfile
echo '/swapfile none swap sw 0 0' >> /etc/fstab

# Docker
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh
usermod -aG docker deploy
```

Log in again as `deploy`.

### 4. Get the code and the settings

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /opt/tenantecom && sudo chown deploy /opt/tenantecom
cd /opt/tenantecom
git clone https://github.com/mudit06/tenantcommerce.git app # a deploy key or token for a private repo
nano /opt/tenantecom/.env.production # the variables from the top of this file
chmod 600 /opt/tenantecom/.env.production
```

The settings file lives outside the git checkout and is never committed (CLAUDE.md rule 9).

### 5. Build and start the app

```bash
cd /opt/tenantecom/app
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t tenantecom:latest .
docker run -d --name tenantecom --restart unless-stopped \
 --env-file /opt/tenantecom/.env.production \
 -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \
 tenantecom:latest
docker logs -f tenantecom # wait for "Ready", then Ctrl+C
```

`127.0.0.1:3000` keeps the app reachable only through Caddy, never directly from the internet.

### 6. HTTPS and the `Host` header: Caddy

Caddy terminates HTTPS, gets a free Let's Encrypt certificate for every address it lists, renews
them, and passes the original `Host` header to the app (which is how the app knows the store).

```bash
sudo apt install -y debian-keyring debian-archive-keyring apt-transport-https curl
curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/gpg.key' | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/caddy-stable-archive-keyring.gpg
curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/debian.deb.txt' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/caddy-stable.list
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y caddy
```

`/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`:

```caddyfile
{
	email ops@tenantecom.in
}

(app) {
	reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
}

# Platform panel and every vendor's CMS
admin.tenantecom.in {
	import app
}

# Bare platform domain: no marketing site yet
tenantecom.in, www.tenantecom.in {
	redir https://admin.tenantecom.in/admin 302
}

# ---- Stores: one block per store ----
# Home Orbit: platform subdomain and its own domain
home-orbit.tenantecom.in, homeorbit.in {
	import app
}
www.homeorbit.in {
	redir https://homeorbit.in{uri} 301
}
cms.homeorbit.in {
	redir https://admin.tenantecom.in/admin 302
}
```

```bash
sudo systemctl reload caddy
```

Caddy needs each address to already point at the server (DNS) and ports 80 and 443 open before it
can get the certificate. `journalctl -u caddy -f` shows progress.

If you use nginx instead of Caddy, keep `proxy_set_header Host $host;` and raise
`client_max_body_size` to 50m (catalogue PDFs, `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` in `src/payload.config.ts`).

### 7. First data

The production image holds only the built app, not the seed scripts, so run the seed once from a
developer machine (a full checkout with `pnpm install`) pointed at the production database. Copy
the production values into a git-ignored file, for example `.env.production.local`, add
`SEED_SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL` and a strong `SEED_SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, then:

```bash
set -a && source .env.production.local && set +a
NODE_ENV=development pnpm seed # plans, the first super admin, 2 demo stores (draft)
NODE_ENV=development pnpm seed:home-orbit # only if Home Orbit's catalogue should be loaded
```

Variables already in the shell win over `.env`, so this writes to Atlas and R2, not to your local
setup. `PLATFORM_DOMAIN` must be the real one here, because new stores get
`<slug>.<PLATFORM_DOMAIN>` as their first address. The demo stores stay in draft and show "coming
soon" in production; archive them from the platform panel if you don't want them.

### 8. Check it

1. `https://admin.tenantecom.in` opens the admin login; sign in as the super admin and change the
 password.
2. `https://home-orbit.tenantecom.in` shows "Home Orbit is coming soon" while the store is in
 draft. Go live from the platform panel (vendor overview, Go live) and reload.
3. Upload an image in the CMS and check its address starts with `MEDIA_PUBLIC_URL`.
4. Walk docs/manual-testing.md against the live addresses.

### 9. Updates

```bash
cd /opt/tenantecom/app && git pull
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t tenantecom:latest .
docker rm -f tenantecom && docker run -d --name tenantecom --restart unless-stopped \
 --env-file /opt/tenantecom/.env.production -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 tenantecom:latest
```

The store is down for the few seconds between `rm` and `run`. When that matters, build the image in
CI, push it to a registry, and switch between two containers behind Caddy. Run Payload migrations
(docs/15) before starting a new version once there are any. Backups are Atlas's (docs/15).

### Without Docker (Node + PM2)

Works too; Docker is preferred because CI keeps the image building (docs/15).

```bash
# Node 22 from NodeSource, then pnpm through corepack
curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_22.x | sudo -E bash - && sudo apt install -y nodejs
sudo corepack enable && sudo npm install -g pm2

cd /opt/tenantecom/app && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
set -a && source /opt/tenantecom/.env.production && set +a && pnpm build
cp -r public .next/standalone/ && cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/
PORT=3000 HOSTNAME=127.0.0.1 pm2 start .next/standalone/server.js --name tenantecom \
 --node-args="--env-file=/opt/tenantecom/.env.production"
pm2 save && pm2 startup # restart on reboot
```

Caddy (step 6) stays the same.

## How vendor addresses reach the right store

There is no per-vendor server and nothing redirects a shopper between stores. Every address
points at the **same app**, and the app reads which address was asked for:

```
 shopper -> https://homeorbit.in/products/basin-mixer
 DNS: homeorbit.in -> 203.0.113.10 (our server)
 Caddy: HTTPS, passes Host: homeorbit.in to the app
 src/proxy.ts: host is not the admin host -> rewrite (not redirect) to /homeorbit.in/products/basin-mixer
 src/lib/data/store.ts getStoreByHost('homeorbit.in'): tenant-domains -> Home Orbit
 src/app/(storefront)/[tenant]: Home Orbit's pages, its data only, its look from
 src/storefront/vendors/home-orbit/

 vendor staff -> https://admin.tenantecom.in/admin
 src/proxy.ts: admin host -> Payload admin
 signed in as Home Orbit staff -> only Home Orbit's CMS (workspaces and access, docs/05)
```

| Address | What it shows | Where it is set |
|---|---|---|
| `admin.tenantecom.in` | Platform panel for our team; the store's CMS for vendor staff | `ADMIN_URL` |
| `<slug>.tenantecom.in` | That vendor's store | Created automatically when the vendor is onboarded (`tenant-domains`, primary) |
| Vendor's own domain | That vendor's store | Added by a super admin in `tenant-domains` (below) |
| Any other address | 404 page | |

The address-to-store map is cached for up to 5 minutes and cleared whenever a domain changes
(docs/04).

### A new vendor's store subdomain

Nothing to do in DNS (the `*` record covers it). Onboard the vendor (New vendor screen or
`pnpm create-tenant`); the store answers on `<slug>.tenantecom.in`. On a VPS add the address to
the Caddyfile so it gets a certificate, then `sudo systemctl reload caddy`.

### A vendor's own domain (for example `homeorbit.in`)

1. **Vendor's DNS** (at their registrar; GoDaddy shown):

 | Type | Name | Value |
 |---|---|---|
 | A | `@` | `203.0.113.10` |
 | CNAME | `www` | `home-orbit.tenantecom.in` |

 GoDaddy can't put a CNAME on the bare domain, so `@` is an A record to the server's IP. If the
 server's IP ever changes, every vendor's `@` record has to change too; a fixed IP for the
 server avoids that.

2. **Tell the app the domain belongs to the store.** Custom domains have no form yet (the
 Domains tab marks it Phase 2). A super admin, in the platform panel (no store session open),
 opens `https://admin.tenantecom.in/admin/collections/tenant-domains/create` and adds `homeorbit.in`:
 tenant Home Orbit, type Custom, Primary ticked (making it primary unticks the subdomain). Add
 `www.homeorbit.in` the same way, not primary, if the store should also answer there instead of
 Caddy redirecting it.

3. **Certificate and routing**: add the domain to the Caddyfile (step 6) and reload Caddy.

4. **One address for search engines**: links, the sitemap and robots.txt use whichever address
 the shopper opened. The stored "redirect to primary" flag is not acted on yet
 (docs/open-items "Primary domain redirect"), so redirect the other addresses in Caddy:
 `www.homeorbit.in` to `homeorbit.in` as above, and, once the vendor's domain is live, the
 subdomain too:

 ```caddyfile
 homeorbit.in {
 	import app
 }
 home-orbit.tenantecom.in, www.homeorbit.in {
 	redir https://homeorbit.in{uri} 301
 }
 ```

### The vendor CMS address

Every vendor signs in at the one admin address, `https://admin.tenantecom.in/admin`. The account
decides what opens: a store's staff get that store's CMS and never see another store; our team
gets the platform panel and reaches a store's CMS only through "Manage store" or "View as support"
(docs/05 "As built"). In production
the admin works only on `ADMIN_URL` (`src/proxy.ts`, CSRF list in
`src/payload.config.ts`).

A vendor who wants a CMS address on their own domain can have a **redirect**: `cms.homeorbit.in`
to `https://admin.tenantecom.in/admin` (the Caddy block above; the vendor adds an A record for
`cms` pointing to the server). Serving the admin itself on each vendor's domain (white-label CMS)
would need code changes (admin host list, CSRF list, sign-in cookies per domain) and is not
planned; raise it in docs/open-items before building it.

## Notes for Vercel instead

- Import the GitHub repo as a Vercel project and set the environment variables, plus
 `S3_CLIENT_UPLOADS=true` (Vercel caps request bodies at 4.5 MB; the bucket needs a CORS rule
 allowing PUT from the admin address).
- Wildcard subdomains (`*.tenantecom.in`) on Vercel need the domain's nameservers moved to Vercel.
- Each vendor domain is added to the project (Settings, Domains); Vercel shows the DNS records and
 issues the certificate. Add the same host to `tenant-domains` as above.
- Background jobs don't run on a timer there: a Vercel Cron for `/api/payload-jobs/run` is still
 to be configured (docs/progress.md, Platform foundations).
- Pick the Mumbai (`bom1`) function region, next to Atlas.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause |
|---|---|
| A store address shows the 404 page | The host is not in `tenant-domains` (check `www.` too), or the store is archived |
| "coming soon" on a store | The store is still in draft: Go live in the platform panel |
| Admin sign-in loops back to the login page | The address in the browser is not exactly `ADMIN_URL`, or `ADMIN_URL` is `http://` while the site is on HTTPS |
| Caddy can't get a certificate | DNS for that address does not point at the server yet, or port 80/443 is closed |
| Uploads fail | `S3_*` variables missing or wrong; the container can't store files on its own disk |
| `MongoServerSelectionError` in `docker logs` | The server's IP is not in Atlas Network Access, or `DATABASE_URI` is wrong |
| The app stops on a small server during build | Not enough memory: add swap (step 3) or build the image elsewhere |

## VPS Server Specifications for TenantEcom

Based on your project's hosting documentation ([docs/19-hosting-and-domains.md](docs/19-hosting-and-domains.md)), here are the **exact requirements**:

### ✅ Minimum VPS Specifications

| Component | Requirement | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Operating System** | **Ubuntu 24.04 LTS** | Tested and documented in your setup guide |
| **CPU** | **2 vCPU** minimum | Handles Next.js build + runtime + background jobs |
| **RAM** | **4 GB** minimum | Running app needs ~1 GB; build needs ~4 GB |
| **Storage** | **40 GB+** disk | Docker images, app code, logs, swap file |
| **Swap** | **4 GB swap file** | Critical if building on the server (prevents out-of-memory crashes during `next build`) |
| **Network** | **Ports 80, 443, 22** open | HTTPS (Caddy), SSH access |
| **Location** | **Closest to Mumbai/India** | Your MongoDB Atlas is in **AWS Mumbai (ap-south-1)** — low latency is critical for every page load |

---

### Scaling Notes

| Scenario | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| **Build separately** (CI/CD builds Docker image, VPS only runs it) | Can drop to **2 GB RAM** on VPS (no swap needed) |
| **High traffic** (100+ vendors or 10K+ daily visitors) | Upgrade to **4 vCPU / 8 GB RAM** |
| **Production-grade** | **8 GB RAM** if you skip swap and want headroom |

---

### Recommended VPS Providers (India-focused)

Since your database is in **Mumbai**, pick the **geographically closest** option:

| Provider | Plan | Location | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **GoDaddy VPS** | Self-managed, 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 40 GB | Check if they offer **Mumbai or Singapore** | Your docs explicitly validate GoDaddy VPS works |
| **AWS Lightsail** | $20/month, 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 80 GB SSD | **Mumbai (ap-south-1)** | Same region as Atlas — lowest latency |
| **DigitalOcean** | $24/month, 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 80 GB | **Bangalore (blr1)** | Close to Mumbai, excellent docs |
| **Hetzner** | €4.49/month, 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 40 GB | **No India datacenter** | Cheapest but high latency to Mumbai Atlas |

**Best choice:** AWS Lightsail Mumbai or DigitalOcean Bangalore — both are **in India** and close to your Atlas cluster.

---

### What Gets Installed on the VPS

Your VPS setup ([docs/19-hosting-and-domains.md](docs/19-hosting-and-domains.md) step 3–6) installs:

1. **Docker** (preferred) — runs your pre-built image
2. **Caddy** — reverse proxy, auto HTTPS certificates, passes `Host` header for multi-tenancy
3. **Swap file** (4 GB) — prevents build crashes
4. **Firewall (UFW)** — locks down everything except ports 22, 80, 443

**Or**, without Docker:
- **Node.js 22** (via NodeSource)
- **pnpm 10** (via `corepack`)
- **PM2** (process manager)

---

### ☁️ External Services (NOT on VPS)

These must be separate cloud accounts (your VPS doesn't host them):

| Service | What | Provider | Why not on VPS |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Database** | MongoDB replica set | **MongoDB Atlas** (Mumbai M10 cluster, ~₹5,000/month) | Payload CMS requires transactions (replica set); backups, scaling handled by Atlas |
| **Object Storage** | Images, PDFs, media | **Cloudflare R2** (~₹500/month) | Docker containers reset disk on update; CDN required |
| **Email** | Transactional (invites, resets) | **Resend** | Staff invites, password resets |
| **DNS** | Domain management | **GoDaddy / Cloudflare** | Points domains to VPS IP |

---

### Quick VPS Checklist (Order When Buying)

When you order the GoDaddy VPS (or any provider), confirm:

- ✅ **Ubuntu 24.04 LTS** (not CentOS, not Debian)
- ✅ **2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, 40+ GB disk**
- ✅ **Root/SSH access** (self-managed, not "managed WordPress" tier)
- ✅ **Static IP included** (most VPS plans include one)
- ✅ **Mumbai / Singapore / Bangalore datacenter** (if GoDaddy offers it; otherwise pick AWS Lightsail Mumbai)

---

### After You Buy the VPS

Your docs have a **complete, copy-paste setup guide** in [docs/19-hosting-and-domains.md](docs/19-hosting-and-domains.md) (steps 1–9). The full flow:

1. Create accounts (Atlas Mumbai, R2, Resend)
2. Point DNS `admin.tenantecom.in` + `*.tenantecom.in` to VPS IP
3. SSH in, add swap, install Docker + Caddy
4. Clone repo, build Docker image, run container
5. Configure Caddy for HTTPS + multi-tenant routing
6. Seed production data from your local machine
7. Deploy updates via `git pull` + rebuild

I can create a **GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline** that automates step 7 (updates) if you'd like — just confirm you're using GitHub.

I attempted to set up the local dev environment for **Tenant-Commerce** but hit prerequisite installation issues that need your attention.

### What was found
- **Node.js, npm, pnpm, and Docker** are **not installed** at all on this machine (checked across PowerShell, Git Bash, Command Prompt, and common install paths — all negative).
- `winget` (Windows Package Manager) **is** available, so I attempted automated installs.

### What happened
1. **Node.js**: The project requires **Node 22** exactly, but `winget`'s `OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS` package currently only resolves to **v24.20.0** (the LTS line has moved on). Installing via winget would give you Node 24, not the required Node 22 — this could cause compatibility issues per the README.

### Why I stopped
- Installing the wrong Node version (24 instead of required 22) could break the project (`pnpm setup:local`, native deps, etc.) — I didn't want to proceed blindly.
- Docker Desktop typically requires a **GUI-driven first-run** (license acceptance, WSL2 backend check, restart) that can't be fully automated from a terminal tool.

2. **Reopen IntelliJ** and open this project
3. Reply **"restarted"** and I'll check again

### Option 2: Manual PATH Check
If restarting doesn't work:

1. **Verify Node.js installation:**
 - Open a **new** PowerShell window (not IntelliJ's terminal)
 - Run: `node --version`
 - Should show: `v22.x.x`

2. **Verify Docker Desktop:**
 - Check if Docker Desktop is **running** (should see whale icon in system tray)
 - In a new PowerShell: `docker --version`

3. **If commands still fail** → Node.js and/or Docker didn't add themselves to PATH during installation

### Option 3: Re-install with PATH
- Uninstall Node.js and Docker
- Re-run installers **as Administrator**
- Ensure "Add to PATH" option is checked

---

**Reply with:**
- **"restarted"** → if you've restarted IntelliJ 
- **"need help"** → if commands still don't work after restart
- **"not installed yet"** → if you haven't finished installing

## Docker Desktop Not Running

The error `500 Internal Server Error for API route http://%2F%2F.%2Fpipe%2FdockerDesktopLinuxEngine` indicates Docker Desktop isn't running or isn't fully started.

### Steps to Fix:

1. **Start Docker Desktop:**
 - Look for Docker Desktop in your Windows Start menu
 - Launch it and wait for it to fully start (this can take 30-60 seconds)
 - You should see the Docker icon in your system tray (bottom-right)
 - Wait until the icon is steady and not animated

2. **Verify Docker is running:**
 ```bash
 docker ps
 ```
 This should return an empty list or show running containers (not an error).

3. **Start MongoDB:**
 ```bash
 docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d mongo
 ```
 Wait about 10 seconds for MongoDB to initialize.

4. **Continue with setup:**
 ```bash
 pnpm install
 pnpm setup:local
 pnpm seed
 pnpm seed:home-orbit
 pnpm dev
 ```

### Common Issues:

- **Docker Desktop not installed**: Download from [docker.com/products/docker-desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop)
- **WSL 2 required**: Docker Desktop on Windows uses WSL 2. If prompted, install/update WSL 2
- **Starting slowly**: Docker Desktop can take a minute to fully start, especially on first launch

Once Docker Desktop is running and `docker ps` works without errors, you'll be able to start the MongoDB container needed for this project.","userText":"PS C:\Users\namgupta5\Downloads\Tenant-Commerce> docker ps

# 19 Hosting and domains

How to put the app on a server, what it needs, whether GoDaddy works, and how each ven…
## ⚠️ cPanel Deployment: Not Suitable

Based on the comprehensive hosting documentation, **cPanel shared hosting cannot run this application**. Here's why and what your options are:

### Why cPanel Won't Work:

1. **Memory Requirements**: Build needs ~4 GB; cPanel shared hosting caps processes at ~1 GB
2. **Node.js Version**: Requires Node 22; cPanel may not support it
3. **Background Jobs**: App runs scheduled tasks that need 24/7 uptime; cPanel's Passenger starts/stops on demand
4. **MongoDB**: Requires a replica set; not available in cPanel
5. **Custom Domains**: Each vendor domain needs manual cPanel configuration with plan limits
6. **No Docker Support**: Cannot use the production Docker image

---

## ✅ Recommended Options for homeorbit.in

### **Option 1: VPS Hosting (Recommended)**
Use a Linux VPS from **any provider** (GoDaddy VPS, AWS Lightsail Mumbai, DigitalOcean Bangalore):

**Requirements:**
- Ubuntu 24.04 LTS
- 2 vCPU, 4-8 GB RAM
- 40 GB+ disk
- Location: Close to Mumbai (database is in Atlas Mumbai)

**Cost estimate:** ₹500-2000/month depending on provider

**What you'll need:**
1. MongoDB Atlas (free M0 tier for testing, M10 for production)
2. Cloudflare R2 for media storage (free tier available)
3. Resend API for emails
4. Domain DNS access

**Deployment steps:** Fully documented in `docs/19-hosting-and-domains.md` (step-by-step guide included)

---

### **Option 2: Vercel + Atlas (Easiest)**
Deploy to Vercel with MongoDB Atlas:

**Advantages:**
- Zero server management
- Automatic SSL for all domains
- Auto-scaling
- Quickest to set up

**Requirements:**
- Vercel account (free tier available, Pro for production)
- MongoDB Atlas
- Cloudflare R2
- Resend API

**Notes:**
- Wildcard subdomains require moving nameservers to Vercel
- Each vendor domain added in Vercel dashboard
- Need to configure Vercel Cron for background jobs

---

2. **Set up Vercel deployment** - Configure for Vercel with step-by-step instructions
3. **Explore alternative hosting** - Research other Node.js-friendly hosts (Render, Railway, Fly.io)

# 19 Hosting and domains

How to put the app on a server, what it needs, whether GoDaddy works, and how each vendor's store
address and CMS address reach the right store. Written 4 October 2026; nothing is deployed yet
(docs/progress.md).

Examples use `tenantecom.in` as the platform domain, `203.0.113.10` as the server's IP address and
Home Orbit (slug `home-orbit`) with an own domain `homeorbit.in`. Swap in the real values.

## What the app needs

One Next.js + Payload app serves every store, the vendor CMS and the platform panel (docs/01). It
needs:

| Need | What exactly | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Node.js | 22.12 or later, below 23 (`package.json` engines) | The Docker image brings its own |
| Memory | About 1 GB for the running app; about 4 GB while building | Build somewhere else, or add swap on a small server |
| MongoDB | A **replica set** (Payload uses transactions) | MongoDB Atlas, Mumbai region: M10 for production, the free M0 is fine for a trial |
| Object storage | An S3-compatible bucket + a public CDN address | Cloudflare R2 recommended (docs/12). Needed on a server too: a container's disk is replaced on every update (the app only warns at boot outside Vercel, `src/lib/mediaStorage.ts`) |
| Email | Resend API key with the sending domain verified | Staff invites and password resets |
| Domain | A platform domain you control | Must not contain "sr", "kr" or "shiprocket" (docs/open-items) |
| HTTPS | A certificate for the admin address, every store subdomain and every vendor domain | Caddy (below) gets and renews them automatically |
| Reverse proxy | Something in front of the app on ports 80/443 that **passes the original `Host` header** | The app picks the store from that header |
| Always-on process | The app runs background jobs on a timer (`jobs.autoRun` in `src/payload.config.ts`) | Fine on a VPS; serverless hosts need a cron instead |

Environment variables are all in `.env.example`. For production:

```bash
NODE_ENV=production
DATABASE_URI=mongodb+srv://<user>:<password>@<cluster>.mongodb.net/tenantecom?retryWrites=true&w=majority
PAYLOAD_SECRET=<openssl rand -hex 32>
ADMIN_URL=https://admin.tenantecom.in
PLATFORM_DOMAIN=tenantecom.in
RESEND_API_KEY=<from Resend>
EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS=no-reply@tenantecom.in
EMAIL_FROM_NAME=TenantEcom
S3_BUCKET=tenantecom-media
S3_ENDPOINT=https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com
S3_REGION=auto
S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID=<R2 token id>
S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=<R2 token secret>
MEDIA_PUBLIC_URL=https://media.tenantecom.in
S3_CLIENT_UPLOADS=false
```

No quotes around values (Docker's `--env-file` keeps quotes as part of the value).

## Where to host it

| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Vercel + Atlas | The recorded decision (docs/00, docs/02). Least work to run; custom domains get SSL automatically. Short notes at the end of this file |
| **A Linux VPS** (GoDaddy VPS, AWS Lightsail Mumbai, DigitalOcean Bangalore, any other) + Atlas | Works, using the Docker image we already keep building (docs/15). Step by step below |
| GoDaddy shared hosting (cPanel "Setup Node.js App") | **Not suitable.** See the next section |

If the team picks a VPS over Vercel for production, record that in docs/00 "Decisions" (CLAUDE.md:
the stack does not change without a recorded decision).

## Can it run on GoDaddy?

**GoDaddy shared hosting / cPanel Node.js: no.** Those plans run small Node apps through Phusion
Passenger with tight limits, and this app does not fit:

- The build needs about 4 GB of memory; shared plans cap a process at around 1 GB or less.
- The Node versions on offer may not include Node 22, which this app requires.
- Passenger starts and stops the app on demand, so the background jobs (scheduled publishing,
 subscription checks, later payments and parcel jobs) would not run reliably.
- No root and no Docker; each vendor's own domain would have to be added as an "addon domain",
 limited per plan, and pointed at the same app by hand.
- MongoDB is not included (Atlas would still be needed).

**GoDaddy VPS: yes.** A self-managed GoDaddy VPS is an ordinary Linux server with root access, so
the steps below work as written. Pick:

- Ubuntu 24.04 LTS
- 2 vCPU and 4 GB RAM at least (8 GB if you build on the same server without swap)
- 40 GB+ disk
- The data centre closest to India that GoDaddy offers. The database sits in Atlas Mumbai, and
 every page makes database calls, so the server should be close to Mumbai. If GoDaddy has no
 nearby location, a Mumbai or Bangalore VPS from another provider is the better choice; the steps
 are the same.

Buying the domain from GoDaddy is fine with any of the options; only the DNS records matter.

## Step by step: a Linux VPS

### 1. Accounts to create first

1. **Platform domain** (for example `tenantecom.in`).
2. **MongoDB Atlas**: create a cluster in AWS Mumbai (`ap-south-1`). Add a database user. Under
 Network Access add the server's IP address (and your own, for step 7). Copy the `mongodb+srv://`
 connection string into `DATABASE_URI`.
3. **Cloudflare R2**: create a bucket (for example `tenantecom-media`), an API token with read and
 write on it, and connect a custom domain to the bucket (for example `media.tenantecom.in`) for
 `MEDIA_PUBLIC_URL`.
4. **Resend**: verify the sending domain, create an API key.

### 2. DNS for the platform domain

In GoDaddy (Domain, DNS, Manage DNS) for `tenantecom.in`:

| Type | Name | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `admin` | `203.0.113.10` | Platform panel and every vendor's CMS |
| A | `*` | `203.0.113.10` | Every store subdomain (`home-orbit.tenantecom.in`, ...) without a DNS change per vendor |
| A | `@` | `203.0.113.10` | The bare domain (redirected to the admin for now, see step 6) |

`media` is set up by Cloudflare when you connect the R2 custom domain (the domain's DNS must be on
Cloudflare for that; otherwise use R2's public `r2.dev` address or put a CDN in front).

### 3. Prepare the server

```bash
ssh root@203.0.113.10
adduser deploy && usermod -aG sudo deploy # work as this user from now on
apt update && apt upgrade -y
ufw allow OpenSSH && ufw allow 80 && ufw allow 443 && ufw enable

# Swap, so building on a 4 GB server does not run out of memory
fallocate -l 4G /swapfile && chmod 600 /swapfile && mkswap /swapfile && swapon /swapfile
echo '/swapfile none swap sw 0 0' >> /etc/fstab

# Docker
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh
usermod -aG docker deploy
```

Log in again as `deploy`.

### 4. Get the code and the settings

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /opt/tenantecom && sudo chown deploy /opt/tenantecom
cd /opt/tenantecom
git clone https://github.com/mudit06/tenantcommerce.git app # a deploy key or token for a private repo
nano /opt/tenantecom/.env.production # the variables from the top of this file
chmod 600 /opt/tenantecom/.env.production
```

The settings file lives outside the git checkout and is never committed (CLAUDE.md rule 9).

### 5. Build and start the app

```bash
cd /opt/tenantecom/app
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t tenantecom:latest .
docker run -d --name tenantecom --restart unless-stopped \
 --env-file /opt/tenantecom/.env.production \
 -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \
 tenantecom:latest
docker logs -f tenantecom # wait for "Ready", then Ctrl+C
```

`127.0.0.1:3000` keeps the app reachable only through Caddy, never directly from the internet.

### 6. HTTPS and the `Host` header: Caddy

Caddy terminates HTTPS, gets a free Let's Encrypt certificate for every address it lists, renews
them, and passes the original `Host` header to the app (which is how the app knows the store).

```bash
sudo apt install -y debian-keyring debian-archive-keyring apt-transport-https curl
curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/gpg.key' | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/caddy-stable-archive-keyring.gpg
curl -1sLf 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/debian.deb.txt' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/caddy-stable.list
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y caddy
```

`/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`:

```caddyfile
{
	email ops@tenantecom.in
}

(app) {
	reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
}

# Platform panel and every vendor's CMS
admin.tenantecom.in {
	import app
}

# Bare platform domain: no marketing site yet
tenantecom.in, www.tenantecom.in {
	redir https://admin.tenantecom.in/admin 302
}

# ---- Stores: one block per store ----
# Home Orbit: platform subdomain and its own domain
home-orbit.tenantecom.in, homeorbit.in {
	import app
}
www.homeorbit.in {
	redir https://homeorbit.in{uri} 301
}
cms.homeorbit.in {
	redir https://admin.tenantecom.in/admin 302
}
```

```bash
sudo systemctl reload caddy
```

Caddy needs each address to already point at the server (DNS) and ports 80 and 443 open before it
can get the certificate. `journalctl -u caddy -f` shows progress.

If you use nginx instead of Caddy, keep `proxy_set_header Host $host;` and raise
`client_max_body_size` to 50m (catalogue PDFs, `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` in `src/payload.config.ts`).

### 7. First data

The production image holds only the built app, not the seed scripts, so run the seed once from a
developer machine (a full checkout with `pnpm install`) pointed at the production database. Copy
the production values into a git-ignored file, for example `.env.production.local`, add
`SEED_SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL` and a strong `SEED_SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, then:

```bash
set -a && source .env.production.local && set +a
NODE_ENV=development pnpm seed # plans, the first super admin, 2 demo stores (draft)
NODE_ENV=development pnpm seed:home-orbit # only if Home Orbit's catalogue should be loaded
```

Variables already in the shell win over `.env`, so this writes to Atlas and R2, not to your local
setup. `PLATFORM_DOMAIN` must be the real one here, because new stores get
`<slug>.<PLATFORM_DOMAIN>` as their first address. The demo stores stay in draft and show "coming
soon" in production; archive them from the platform panel if you don't want them.

### 8. Check it

1. `https://admin.tenantecom.in` opens the admin login; sign in as the super admin and change the
 password.
2. `https://home-orbit.tenantecom.in` shows "Home Orbit is coming soon" while the store is in
 draft. Go live from the platform panel (vendor overview, Go live) and reload.
3. Upload an image in the CMS and check its address starts with `MEDIA_PUBLIC_URL`.
4. Walk docs/manual-testing.md against the live addresses.

### 9. Updates

```bash
cd /opt/tenantecom/app && git pull
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t tenantecom:latest .
docker rm -f tenantecom && docker run -d --name tenantecom --restart unless-stopped \
 --env-file /opt/tenantecom/.env.production -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 tenantecom:latest
```

The store is down for the few seconds between `rm` and `run`. When that matters, build the image in
CI, push it to a registry, and switch between two containers behind Caddy. Run Payload migrations
(docs/15) before starting a new version once there are any. Backups are Atlas's (docs/15).

### Without Docker (Node + PM2)

Works too; Docker is preferred because CI keeps the image building (docs/15).

```bash
# Node 22 from NodeSource, then pnpm through corepack
curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_22.x | sudo -E bash - && sudo apt install -y nodejs
sudo corepack enable && sudo npm install -g pm2

cd /opt/tenantecom/app && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
set -a && source /opt/tenantecom/.env.production && set +a && pnpm build
cp -r public .next/standalone/ && cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/
PORT=3000 HOSTNAME=127.0.0.1 pm2 start .next/standalone/server.js --name tenantecom \
 --node-args="--env-file=/opt/tenantecom/.env.production"
pm2 save && pm2 startup # restart on reboot
```

Caddy (step 6) stays the same.

## How vendor addresses reach the right store

There is no per-vendor server and nothing redirects a shopper between stores. Every address
points at the **same app**, and the app reads which address was asked for:

```
 shopper -> https://homeorbit.in/products/basin-mixer
 DNS: homeorbit.in -> 203.0.113.10 (our server)
 Caddy: HTTPS, passes Host: homeorbit.in to the app
 src/proxy.ts: host is not the admin host -> rewrite (not redirect) to /homeorbit.in/products/basin-mixer
 src/lib/data/store.ts getStoreByHost('homeorbit.in'): tenant-domains -> Home Orbit
 src/app/(storefront)/[tenant]: Home Orbit's pages, its data only, its look from
 src/storefront/vendors/home-orbit/

 vendor staff -> https://admin.tenantecom.in/admin
 src/proxy.ts: admin host -> Payload admin
 signed in as Home Orbit staff -> only Home Orbit's CMS (workspaces and access, docs/05)
```

| Address | What it shows | Where it is set |
|---|---|---|
| `admin.tenantecom.in` | Platform panel for our team; the store's CMS for vendor staff | `ADMIN_URL` |
| `<slug>.tenantecom.in` | That vendor's store | Created automatically when the vendor is onboarded (`tenant-domains`, primary) |
| Vendor's own domain | That vendor's store | Added by a super admin in `tenant-domains` (below) |
| Any other address | 404 page | |

The address-to-store map is cached for up to 5 minutes and cleared whenever a domain changes
(docs/04).

### A new vendor's store subdomain

Nothing to do in DNS (the `*` record covers it). Onboard the vendor (New vendor screen or
`pnpm create-tenant`); the store answers on `<slug>.tenantecom.in`. On a VPS add the address to
the Caddyfile so it gets a certificate, then `sudo systemctl reload caddy`.

### A vendor's own domain (for example `homeorbit.in`)

1. **Vendor's DNS** (at their registrar; GoDaddy shown):

 | Type | Name | Value |
 |---|---|---|
 | A | `@` | `203.0.113.10` |
 | CNAME | `www` | `home-orbit.tenantecom.in` |

 GoDaddy can't put a CNAME on the bare domain, so `@` is an A record to the server's IP. If the
 server's IP ever changes, every vendor's `@` record has to change too; a fixed IP for the
 server avoids that.

2. **Tell the app the domain belongs to the store.** Custom domains have no form yet (the
 Domains tab marks it Phase 2). A super admin, in the platform panel (no store session open),
 opens `https://admin.tenantecom.in/admin/collections/tenant-domains/create` and adds `homeorbit.in`:
 tenant Home Orbit, type Custom, Primary ticked (making it primary unticks the subdomain). Add
 `www.homeorbit.in` the same way, not primary, if the store should also answer there instead of
 Caddy redirecting it.

3. **Certificate and routing**: add the domain to the Caddyfile (step 6) and reload Caddy.

4. **One address for search engines**: links, the sitemap and robots.txt use whichever address
 the shopper opened. The stored "redirect to primary" flag is not acted on yet
 (docs/open-items "Primary domain redirect"), so redirect the other addresses in Caddy:
 `www.homeorbit.in` to `homeorbit.in` as above, and, once the vendor's domain is live, the
 subdomain too:

 ```caddyfile
 homeorbit.in {
 	import app
 }
 home-orbit.tenantecom.in, www.homeorbit.in {
 	redir https://homeorbit.in{uri} 301
 }
 ```

### The vendor CMS address

Every vendor signs in at the one admin address, `https://admin.tenantecom.in/admin`. The account
decides what opens: a store's staff get that store's CMS and never see another store; our team
gets the platform panel and reaches a store's CMS only through "Manage store" or "View as support"
(docs/05 "As built"). In production
the admin works only on `ADMIN_URL` (`src/proxy.ts`, CSRF list in
`src/payload.config.ts`).

A vendor who wants a CMS address on their own domain can have a **redirect**: `cms.homeorbit.in`
to `https://admin.tenantecom.in/admin` (the Caddy block above; the vendor adds an A record for
`cms` pointing to the server). Serving the admin itself on each vendor's domain (white-label CMS)
would need code changes (admin host list, CSRF list, sign-in cookies per domain) and is not
planned; raise it in docs/open-items before building it.

## Notes for Vercel instead

- Import the GitHub repo as a Vercel project and set the environment variables, plus
 `S3_CLIENT_UPLOADS=true` (Vercel caps request bodies at 4.5 MB; the bucket needs a CORS rule
 allowing PUT from the admin address).
- Wildcard subdomains (`*.tenantecom.in`) on Vercel need the domain's nameservers moved to Vercel.
- Each vendor domain is added to the project (Settings, Domains); Vercel shows the DNS records and
 issues the certificate. Add the same host to `tenant-domains` as above.
- Background jobs don't run on a timer there: a Vercel Cron for `/api/payload-jobs/run` is still
 to be configured (docs/progress.md, Platform foundations).
- Pick the Mumbai (`bom1`) function region, next to Atlas.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause |
|---|---|
| A store address shows the 404 page | The host is not in `tenant-domains` (check `www.` too), or the store is archived |
| "coming soon" on a store | The store is still in draft: Go live in the platform panel |
| Admin sign-in loops back to the login page | The address in the browser is not exactly `ADMIN_URL`, or `ADMIN_URL` is `http://` while the site is on HTTPS |
| Caddy can't get a certificate | DNS for that address does not point at the server yet, or port 80/443 is closed |
| Uploads fail | `S3_*` variables missing or wrong; the container can't store files on its own disk |
| `MongoServerSelectionError` in `docker logs` | The server's IP is not in Atlas Network Access, or `DATABASE_URI` is wrong |
| The app stops on a small server during build | Not enough memory: add swap (step 3) or build the image elsewhere |

## What was wrong

On line 53:

```ts
.replace(/\/g, '/') // ❌ broken
```

The regex `/\/g` is interpreted as:
- `/` → start of regex
- `\/` → an escaped forward slash (one character)
- `g` → part of the pattern

...which leaves the regex literal **never closed**, so esbuild/tsx throws `Unterminated string literal` at `53:80`.

## The fix

```ts
.replace(/\\/g, '/') // ✅ correct
```

A backslash in a regex must be escaped as `\\`. Now the pattern correctly matches Windows path separators (`\`) and replaces them with `/`.

## What was wrong

On line 53:

```ts
.replace(/\/g, '/') // ❌ broken
```

The regex `/\/g` is interpreted as:
- `/` → start of regex
- `\/` → an escaped forward slash (one character)
- `g` → part of the pattern

...which leaves the regex literal **never closed**, so esbuild/tsx throws `Unterminated string literal` at `53:80`.

## The fix

```ts
.replace(/\\/g, '/') // ✅ correct
```

A backslash in a regex must be escaped as `\\`. Now the pattern correctly matches Windows path separators (`\`) and replaces them with `/`.

## Files Modified
- [simple-r2-upload.ts](scripts/simple-r2-upload.ts) — Fixed unterminated regex literal on line 53 (`/\/g` → `/\\/g`) +1 −1 lines

You can re-run:

```bash
pnpm exec tsx scripts/simple-r2-upload.ts
```

Let me explain why, based on your script and the data structure.

## What your script actually touches

Looking at your script, the MongoDB update section only touches **one collection**:

```ts
const mediaCollection = db.collection('media') // ← only the "media" collection
...
await mediaCollection.updateOne(
 { _id: record._id },
 { $set: { url: r2Url } } // ← only sets the "url" field
)
```

So the script:
1. Uploads physical files to R2.
2. In the **`media` collection**, sets each record's `url` field to `https://<PUBLIC_DOMAIN>/<filename>`.

It **never writes to the `products` collection.**

## Why the product doesn't change

Your product document references images **by ID, not by URL**:

```json
"gallery": [
 { "$oid": "6ad1d2d85b5173a443507cb7" } // ← a reference to a media document's _id
]
```

The `gallery` array stores an **ObjectId relation** pointing into the `media` collection. The actual URL lives on the media document, not the product. So changing the media record's `url` is enough — the product keeps pointing to the same `_id`.

## What changes (in the `media` collection)

The media document with `_id: 6ad1d2d85b5173a443507cb7` is what gets updated:

**Before**
```json
{
 "_id": { "$oid": "6ad1d2d85b5173a443507cb7" },
 "filename": "some-image.jpg",
 "url": "/media/some-image.jpg" // or a local/old URL
}
```

**After**
```json
{
 "_id": { "$oid": "6ad1d2d85b5173a443507cb7" },
 "filename": "some-image.jpg",
 "url": "https://<your-r2-public-domain>/some-image.jpg" // ← updated
}
```

## Flow summary

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 A[products.gallery<br/>$oid ref] -->|points to _id| B[media document]
 B -->|script updates| C[url field → R2 URL]
 D[Local file in /media] -->|uploaded| E[Cloudflare R2 bucket]
```

## Important caveats to check

1. **Payload/`sizes` variants not handled** — Payload CMS media docs usually also store resized variants (e.g. `sizes.thumbnail.url`, `sizes.card.url`). Your script only updates the top-level `url`, so those nested URLs will still point to the old location. You may need to update those too.
2. **`filename` with subfolders** — Your R2 `Key` uses the relative path (which may include subfolders), but the DB update uses `${PUBLIC_DOMAIN}/${record.filename}`. If files were uploaded under a subfolder but `filename` has no folder prefix, the URLs won't match the R2 keys.

So: **the product stays exactly as-is** — only the linked `media` record's `url` is rewritten to the R2 domain.

# Every variable the app reads, documented. `pnpm setup:local` creates .env from this file and
# generates the secrets; or copy it by hand. Never commit .env.
# Validated at boot by src/lib/env.ts; the app refuses to start when a required one is missing.

# ---- Core ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MongoDB connection. Must be a replica set (transactions). Local: docker/docker-compose.yml
DATABASE_URI=mongodb://localhost:27017/tenantecom?replicaSet=rs0&directConnection=true
# Signs Payload JWTs and cookies. At least 32 random characters: `openssl rand -hex 32`
PAYLOAD_SECRET=
# Public URL of the admin app (our team and vendor staff sign in here). Used for links in
# staff invite emails and as Payload's serverURL. Locally plain localhost works in every browser.
ADMIN_URL=http://localhost:3000
# Platform domain: every new store gets <slug>.<PLATFORM_DOMAIN> as its first address.
# Must not contain "sr", "kr" or "shiprocket" in production (Shiprocket webhook rule, docs/open-items).
PLATFORM_DOMAIN=localhost

# ---- Staff email (invites, password resets) --------------------------------------------
# Leave RESEND_API_KEY empty locally: emails are then printed to the server log (dev-log style).
RESEND_API_KEY=
EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS=no-reply@tenantecom.in
EMAIL_FROM_NAME=TenantEcom

# ---- Media storage ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Leave empty locally: uploads are saved to ./media on disk (gitignored). In production the app
# refuses to start on Vercel without a bucket, and warns elsewhere (src/lib/mediaStorage.ts).
# Each store's files go to their own folder, media/<store id>/ (docs/12 "Media").
# In staging and production, photos and PDFs go to object storage and shoppers load them from a
# CDN, never from the app server or the database (docs/12 "Media"). Cloudflare R2 recommended
# (no charge for downloads); any S3-compatible bucket works.
S3_BUCKET=
# R2: https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com ; AWS S3: leave empty
S3_ENDPOINT=
# R2: auto ; AWS: the bucket's region, for example ap-south-1 (Mumbai)
S3_REGION=auto
S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID=
S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=
# Public CDN address of the bucket (R2 custom domain or CloudFront), for example
# https://media.tenantecom.in . When set, file links point there and skip the app server.
MEDIA_PUBLIC_URL=
# true on Vercel: the browser uploads straight to the bucket (Vercel caps request bodies at 4.5 MB).
# Needs a CORS rule on the bucket allowing PUT from the admin address.
S3_CLIENT_UPLOADS=false

# ---- Seed (pnpm seed) -------------------------------------------------------------------
# First super admin created by the seed script. Change the password after first sign-in.
SEED_SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@tenantecom.local
SEED_SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD=

# ---- Tests ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Optional. Integration tests start mongodb-memory-server unless this points at a running
# replica set (for example the docker compose one). Each test file uses its own database.
MONGODB_TEST_URI=

# ---- Connectors (payment, shipping, WhatsApp; docs/09) ---------------------------------
# Encrypts every vendor's connector secrets at rest, AES-256-GCM, 32 bytes base64 (docs/14):
# `openssl rand -base64 32`. Required in production and never changed once keys are saved
# (saved keys could no longer be read). `pnpm setup:local` generates one.
CONNECTOR_ENC_KEY=
# Local only: `pnpm demo:selling <store>` connects Razorpay in test mode with these
# RAZORPAY_TEST_KEY_ID=
# RAZORPAY_TEST_KEY_SECRET=
# RAZORPAY_TEST_WEBHOOK_SECRET=
# Meta Graph API version used for WhatsApp messages and templates
META_GRAPH_API_VERSION=v21.0

# ---- Later sprints (documented now, not read yet) ---------------------------------------
# Resend webhook signature (docs/04, docs/18)
# RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET=
# Platform Meta app, Phase 2 self-serve WhatsApp (docs/09)
# META_APP_SECRET=

## Why your record still had `/api/media/file/...`

Two independent bugs, both now fixed:

### 1. Wrong environment variable names (the main reason)
Your script read `CLOUDFLARE_R2_BUCKET_NAME`, `CLOUDFLARE_R2_PUBLIC_DOMAIN`, etc., but **this project uses `S3_*` and `MEDIA_PUBLIC_URL`** (confirmed in [.env.example](.env.example)). So `PUBLIC_DOMAIN` was `undefined`, and even when the update ran it would have written garbage like `undefined/HO-BS-15.webp`. Now it uses the correct names and **fails fast** if any are missing.

### 2. Size variants were never updated
The old code only did `{ $set: { url: r2Url } }`. Your media doc has three nested variants:

```
sizes.thumb.url
sizes.card.url
sizes.detail.url
```

These were **never touched** — so they'd stay `/api/media/file/...` forever. The new loop rewrites all of them.

## What your record will look like after re-running

Assuming `MEDIA_PUBLIC_URL=https://media.tenantecom.in` and no store prefix:

```json
"url": "https://media.tenantecom.in/HO-BS-15.webp",
"sizes": {
 "thumb": { "url": "https://media.tenantecom.in/HO-BS-15-200x161.webp", ... },
 "card": { "url": "https://media.tenantecom.in/HO-BS-15-600x484.webp", ... },
 "detail": { "url": "https://media.tenantecom.in/HO-BS-15-713x575.webp", ... }
}
```

## ⚠️ One thing you MUST verify — the store-folder prefix

The `.env.example` says:
> Each store's files go to their own folder, **`media/<store id>/`**

This means your R2 **object key** is likely `<store-id>/HO-BS-15.webp`, but your upload script uploads using the path relative to the local `media/` folder. So:

- If your local files sit in `media/<store-id>/HO-BS-15.webp`, the R2 key becomes `<store-id>/HO-BS-15.webp` ✅
- But the DB `filename` is just `HO-BS-15.webp` (no folder).

My fix reads a `record.prefix` field (Payload stores the folder there) to rebuild the path. **Please confirm whether your media documents have a `prefix` field** — the sample you pasted didn't include one, which could mean:
- files were uploaded to R2 at the bucket root (no prefix), OR
- the prefix exists but you trimmed it from the paste.

Cloudflare Dashboard → **R2** → *(your bucket)* → **Settings** → **Public access** → **Custom Domains**.

### 2. Test the raw endpoint to isolate the problem

### 4. Confirm `CLOUDFLARE_R2_PUBLIC_DOMAIN` in `.env`

If you just added the custom domain, allow a few minutes and hard-refresh (DNS + Cloudflare edge cache).

## The correct architecture: use YOUR OWN platform domain, not a tenant's

Use **one neutral domain that belongs to the platform/application**, not to any tenant. For example:


Only if you want **white-labeled CDN URLs per tenant** (each tenant sees their own brand in image URLs).
